items.q: What is Graham's Treasury-stress story actually about?
items.a: **Rollover + buybacks**, not a clean payoff. From **Sept 9** he says Treasury **doubles** buybacks: issue **new debt to repurchase old** because private demand is thinning. Analogy: pay a mortgage with an **intro-rate credit card**.

items.q: What line on the 10-year does he watch?
items.a: The **5% barrier** — last hit in **2007**, his "everything is fine / something breaks" border. Treat magnitudes as **video claims**, not audited data.

items.q: How does new Chair Warsh differ from Powell, in this telling?
items.a: **Silent-Fed doctrine**: say nothing, let markets move, then act — end the hall of mirrors. Markets pricing **>60%** odds of a **25 bp** hike on **Sept 16**, one week after the buyback step-up.

**No.** September is historically weak (~**45%** positive, avg **−0.6%**). Base case: **5–12%** chop, then sit. Mix: **~55% stocks / 20% munis / 10% Bitcoin ETF / rest real estate**. Dalio "point of no return" is an **intro hook**, not a cycle lecture.
